how_we_lost: P3 (Giada) exploded: Sol Ring T1, Giada round 2, Lyra round 3, Serra Paragon + Resplendent Angel round 4. By round 5 P3 had about 60 flying power and 78 life. We never cast Muldrotha (no ramp drawn, 7 lands by round 8). Our one real out was Toxic Deluge on round 7 (T28), with the memo specifying X=10. Forge resolved it at X of about 0: P3's board was identical afterwards, and even Giada 2/2 and P2's Augur of Autumn 2/3 survived. After that, Battle Angels of Tyr's myriad copy hit us for 11 twice (T31, T34), and Hearthhull's land-sacrifice drain took 8 on T33. P3's 70-power Angel swing killed us on T36.
winnable_why: The opener was 4 lands plus Lantern, Mulldrifter, Dalek Drone and Vrock: no ramp and nothing under 5 MV that interacts. P3 had lethal-scale air before our 6th land. The one real line was Toxic Deluge X=10 on T28 (we were at 31). That kills every Angel (Battle Angels was 10/10) plus Korvold, Moraug and Scarab God, and would have left us favoured with Hostage Taker, Vrock, Galactus and Massacre Wurm in hand. That line was lost to Forge's X choice, not to a pilot decision.

mistakes.what_happened: Toxic Deluge was cast per the memo (X=10), but Forge picked X of about 0. Every creature on the table survived, including Giada 2/2 and Augur of Autumn 2/3, and P3's board was unchanged.
mistakes.better_play: X=10 (pay 10 of our 31 life). That kills all of P3's Angels, Korvold, Moraug and Scarab God.
mistakes.why: It was the only answer to a 60-power flying board. With it wasted, we were dead in two P3 turns.

mistakes.what_happened: After the Deluge did nothing, Hostage Taker still followed the memo, which assumed the Angels were dead. The executor overruled Forge's target (an 8/8 Angel token) and took P3's Sol Ring. No escalation fired, even though P3's board was unchanged.
mistakes.better_play: Take Battle Angels of Tyr, a nontoken 10/10 flier with myriad that we could then cast ourselves, or at least the biggest Angel.
mistakes.why: Battle Angels' myriad copy dealt 11 to us on T31 and again on T34. Sol Ring was irrelevant with no board. The pilot lacked a 'did the wipe actually resolve as planned?' check.

mistakes.what_happened: The executor overruled Forge's 'don't attack' and sent Dalek Drone, the memo's designated chump blocker, at P1 (6 life) into untapped Teval 4/4 and a Lyra token 4/4. Drone was double-blocked and died. P1's Scarab God reanimated it the next turn, and its ETB drained us 3.
mistakes.better_play: Keep Drone home as the memo said.
mistakes.why: It gave away a blocker and fed an opponent's reanimation engine for no damage.

mistakes.what_happened: The executor overruled 'don't attack' again. Hostage Taker attacked P1 (3 life, who was going to die to Vrock's end-step drain anyway) into an untapped Scarab God and died.
mistakes.better_play: No attack. Vrock alone kills P1 at the end step.
mistakes.why: A free creature lost, and a body left for Scarab God.

mistakes.what_happened: The Coming of Galactus was held from T16 to the end. On T24 (6 lands) the memo chose Mulldrifter plus Seal of Doom, although Hearthhull had just stationed to 8 counters and Seal can't hit it (it is black). On T32 the 5 mana went to Vrock to finish P1 at 3, who was already being killed by P3's attacks.
mistakes.better_play: Galactus chapter I on Hearthhull (T24) or on Battle Angels (T32). Killing P1 did nothing for our survival.
mistakes.why: Hearthhull's land-sacrifice drain took 8 from us on T33. It was not decisive against 70 flying power, but it was an answer sitting in hand while threats landed.

mistakes.what_happened: Soul-Guide Lantern was sacrificed on our own turn. The memo said to use it only in response to Living Death or Reanimate, or once P1's yard reached 8+ cards. P1 then used The Scarab God on the graveyards: Spore Frog, Lyra, Dalek Drone and Mulldrifter were all reanimated for P1.
mistakes.better_play: Keep Lantern until Scarab God's first activation, then exile all opposing graveyards in response.
mistakes.why: It was the only graveyard hate we drew, against the opponent whose dossier flags reanimation.

strategy_assessment: The memos read the key facts correctly. Lyra was the right first Drone target: it strips the anthem and lifelink, which is better than hitting the biggest token. They also recognised early that only a sweeper beats P3's board. But the plan kept assuming Muldrotha by turn 6 on a hand with no ramp. Once P3 had 30+ flying power on round 4, the orientation should have switched to survival until a sweeper: keep every blocker home, spend Galactus and Seal on the biggest fliers or Hearthhull as soon as mana allows, and stop spending resources on killing P1, who was already dying to P3. The loss itself came from Forge choosing X of about 0 for Toxic Deluge, which the pilot could not control. That is a harness issue to fix before trusting any sim of this deck, since Deluge is one of its four sweepers.
summary: P3's Angels went wide and huge by round 4 while we had no ramp and no cheap interaction. Muldrotha was never cast. The one out, Toxic Deluge on T28, resolved with Forge-chosen X of about 0 and killed nothing. Hostage Taker then took Sol Ring instead of an Angel because the plan wasn't updated. Secondary executor errors were pointless attacks with Drone and Hostage Taker, and Lantern wasted before Scarab God arrived.
